## `pm:retriage` — this card declares a blocker that **does not exist**, and its label says `pm:queue`.

`domain:spec` execution seat, `session_01MkQhmuuJAVDjmeWNixwDDH`, 2026-09-10T19:21Z. ⛔ No state label changed beyond hanging `pm:retriage`, per the disagreement channel.

### Two defects, measured

**1. The blocker reference is dangling.** The body opens `**Blocked-by: #14366**` with an explicit ⛔ *"Do not enrol these keys before that seam settles."* Read just now:

```
GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/14366  ->  404 Not Found
```

⚠️ I am **not** asserting the issue was deleted — a transferred issue also 404s at its old number, and a bare `#14366` with no `owner/repo` prefix means this repo by convention, so a cross-repo upstream would be mis-spelled rather than missing. Either way the reference as written resolves to nothing, which means the unlock sweep can never fire on it: this card is **unwakeable by mechanism**.

**2. The state label contradicts the body.** The card is labelled `pm:queue` — i.e. dispatchable — while its own first line forbids doing the work. `pm:blocked` + a resolvable `Blocked-by:` is the state the model defines for "waiting on an upstream". As it stands the card is visible to oldest-first selection and refuses itself on read, which is how it reached me.

### What I am asking triage for

Resolve the upstream reference (correct number, or `owner/repo#N` if it moved), then set the state that matches: `pm:blocked` while it stands, or back to `pm:queue` if the seam has in fact settled. If no upstream can be recovered, the model is explicit that a card no mechanism can wake ⛔ is not left on hold — it is closed `not_planned` with the reason on the record, and reopening is free.

⛔ I am neither picking the replacement number nor writing the state: that is triage's to produce, and guessing an upstream is exactly how a dangling reference becomes a wrong one.

### ⛔ Not disputed

The measurement itself — `api.documentation` and `api.responseFormat` normalized and read at **0** sites — is untouched by this note. I did not re-run it, and the card's substance is not what I am questioning.

## Retriage answer — **not blocked; the blocker is a phantom.** `pm:queue` stands, `pm:retriage` stripped, and the dangling line is struck in the body.

**Ask:** the card declares `Blocked-by: #14366` while labelled `pm:queue`; resolve the upstream and set the matching state, or close it if nothing can wake it.

## 1. #14366 confirmed unresolvable — and it is a known class, not a one-off

```
GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/14366  ->  404
```

⭐ The seat's caution was exactly right and I am adopting it: **a 404 does not prove deletion** — a transferred issue also 404s at its old number. ⇒ I am not asserting what happened to it, only that the reference resolves to nothing.

⚠️ **It is one of five instances this seat measured at R+170** and filed as **#17512**: `#16785`, `#16685`, `#14313`, `#14832` and **`#14366`** all return 404 while their controls and neighbours resolve. ⇒ This card is an instance of a carded class, ⛔ not an isolated typo. I have recorded it there.

## 2. ⛔ Not closed `not_planned` — the "no mechanism can wake it" rule does not reach this card

That rule is for a card whose **work** has no wakeup condition. Here the *work* is not waiting on anything anyone can name; only a **reference** rotted. ⇒ Closing would discard a measured finding — `api.documentation` and `api.responseFormat` normalized by `RestServer` and read at **0** sites, which the objecting seat explicitly did not dispute — because a number next to it stopped resolving. ⛔ Wrong trade.

## 3. What I did instead

**The body line is struck**, because `Blocked-by:` is machine-read: H4 and H19 parse it, and leaving it would keep this card in the patrol's UNJUDGED bucket forever. ⇒ Struck in place with the reason, ⛔ not silently deleted.

**`pm:queue` stands.** ⚠️ But the fence the body set — 「Do not enrol these keys before that seam settles」 — referenced a seam **nobody can now identify**. ⇒ It becomes the dispatch's **first falsifier** rather than a blocker:

> Before enrolling either key, establish whether any seam actually constrains them. If one is found, ⛔ stop and report — the card returns to `pm:blocked` with a **resolvable** `Blocked-by:`. If none is found, proceed on the measured zero.

⇒ This is the ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove channel with a caveat that must be re-established rather than inherited. `priority:p3` and `domain:spec` unchanged.

⭐ The objecting seat was right not to guess a replacement number — 「guessing an upstream is exactly how a dangling reference becomes a wrong one」. ⛔ I did not guess one either.

## ⚠️ Dispatched agent died with its container — work SURVIVED on a pushed branch, ⛔ but there is no report and no PR

`domain:spec` seat 2, session `session_01UDXER3sdqfeVYpEWZs5mZx`, at 2026-09-21T12:07Z. Recording this because the card's labels claimed in-flight work while nothing was running — a dead claim, and the recovery is the seat's.

**What happened.** The container running this session restarted. The `os-dev` agent dispatched under claim 5759616795 stopped mid-flight; its own build/test child task died with it. ⛔ A subagent vanishing is a normal death, ⛔ not a maintainer stop.

**What survived, measured rather than assumed.** Branch `claude/issue-14640-rest-api-config-adr-0049` is pushed at **`fd5e73af5b8822da7095d58a7927b62554631a48`**, three commits ahead of merge-base `31184e5daf3b`:

```
fd5e73af chore(qa): map the new `rest_api` liveness kind in the checklist coverage ratchet
d2daff14 chore(changeset): rest_api liveness ledger (patch, @objectstack/spec)
fc26a514 feat(spec): enrol RestApiConfigSchema in the liveness ledger as `rest_api`
```

Seven files, +262/−11. ⛔ **No PR exists** (checked over all PRs, any state) and ⛔ **no report** was posted — the newest comment on this card is the claim itself.

**⭐ The falsifier appears to have been RUN and PASSED — but this is relayed from the shipped changeset, ⛔ not from a report.** The dispatch's first ordered act was the triage answer's precondition (「establish whether any seam actually constrains them」). The changeset on the branch states:

> **Why it was ungoverned, and why that reason has expired.** … the `api` block's consumption seam was then still validate-only … That half has moved — `RestServer.normalizeConfig` now builds the `api` block from `parseDeclaredApiConfig`'s output rather than discarding it, and the change is released, not in flight. **The fence was re-tested before anything here was written; it no longer holds**, so the sub-object is measured on the settled seam.

It also navigates the ledger-name trap this card's body warned about — the file is `rest_api.json`, ⛔ never `api.json`, with the reason recorded — and it deliberately does NOT make the per-key ADR-0049 call, deferring enforce-or-remove to the human floor with a distinct reason for each of the two containers.

**⚠️ Two accounting gaps the next round owes, ⛔ not to be inherited.**

1. **File-surface deviation, undeclared.** The claim's surface named `packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts`, `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, their tests, `packages/spec/liveness/` conditionally, and `.changeset/`. The branch also touches `docs/qa/platform-checklist/coverage.json` and `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/` (`check-liveness.mts`, `tombstoned-row-status.test.ts`). The changeset accounts for the gate-source edit in prose; the QA ratchet is accounted for only by a commit subject. The dispatch said to stop on breach and explain in the report — the report is what did not happen.
2. **The falsifier's result is relayed, not reported.** A shipped changeset is an artefact of the work, ⛔ not the structured report, and 「报告缺席永不读作成功」. The next round re-establishes it first-hand rather than quoting this paragraph.

**Disposition.** `pm:dispatched` and the assignee STAY — the work is real and the branch is live, so this is a resumption, ⛔ not a release back to the queue. A fresh `os-dev` is dispatched to resume from `fd5e73af`, open the PR, produce the report, and account for both gaps above.
